thread:
mohit: noticing a p99 spike in hosted-us-east1 around 11:12 UTC, p95 up ~80ms, p99 jumped to ~1.2s. Affected model: redwood-open-7b-quant.
kara: seeing same in dashboards, queue depth for router-service up from 4->28, backend latency also increased.
anya: any deploys in the last hour?
sre-bot: deploy: kernel-selector v2.3 rolled at 10:55 UTC to 10% hosts (by canary).
mohit: that lines up. kselector change was trying a new short-seq heuristic for kernel affinity.
lucas: logs show kselector flip events spiking, many requests falling back to aux kernel which is ~3x slower for this model. Snippet: 
```
[kselector] chose aux_kernel for model redwood-open-7b-quant seq=32 reason=heuristic_mismatch
kernel_time_ms=210.4
```
jess: KV cache metrics: eviction rate jumped ~6x at the same time, cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 64%. Could be priming thrash.
anya: do we have tenant-level correlation? noisy-tenant detection?
mohit: tenant_id=acct-42 shows disproportionate traffic spike (many short chat messages), batching sampler looks overloaded.
lucas: perf profiler (flame graph) attached — large time spent in aux kernel matmul. Also backlog shows coalescer waiting on KV prefetch locks.
kara: runbook check: if kselector can cause p99, rollback canary or route these tenants to stable selector. Suggestions?
jess: quick mitigation: 1) pin high-traffic tenants to stable kernel, 2) increase pool size for redwood-open-7b-quant, 3) reduce coalescer wait timeout.
anya: I can flip routing rule to prefer stable kernel for prod-tenants. Want me to do it?
mohit: yes, do it for acct-42 and acct-7. Also bump canary->0% for kselector for now.
deploy-bot: routing-rule update requested by anya at 11:32 UTC — in progress.
sre-bot: canary rollback of kernel-selector v2.3 requested by mohit at 11:33 UTC — scheduled.
lucas: after routing change p95 dropped back to ~45ms in ~2 minutes, p99 trending down but still noisy. Queue depth from 28 -> 6.
kara: KV eviction rate stabilizing, cache hit back to ~88% after 4m.
jess: check if batching sampler parameters were changed by selector (we saw sampler aggressively coalesce short-seq into larger batches). That can increase latency for tail.
mohit: confirmed kselector had a patch that preferred larger coalesced batches for short seqs; it increased batch size but also increased variance and contention. revert that too.
anya: rolling back sampler preference now.
deploy-bot: rollback sampler-pref change applied at 11:38 UTC.
lucas: profiler after mitigations shows aux kernel usage down 92% and main kernel restored. p99 now ~210ms.
kara: action items: 1) revert kselector heuristic permanently until we test more, 2) run a load test reproducing short-seq hottenants, 3) add tenant-level circuit-breaker to avoid cross-tenant priming storms, 4) add metric alert for kselector_fallback_rate > 1% over 5m.
jess: I'll own tenant circuit-breaker design.
mohit: I'll own kselector revert + improved unit tests for sampler interplay.
anya: will follow up with postmortem draft in #postmortems with timelines and graphs.
sre-bot: incident closed for mitigation at 11:46 UTC (p99 reduced and queue depth stable).
kara: thanks all — please paste any traces/heatmaps into the postmortem thread. :thumbsup:
